---

  This document summarizes the interagency trawl program results from August of `r this_year`, combining Ontario MNRF and Ohio DOW trawl catches to obtain Western Basin estimates of fish per hectare. These should be considered preliminary data and **should not be shared with the public**. 
  
  
### Methods 
  Briefly, trawl catches are transformed to catch per hectare using trawl distance and SCANMAR-derived, vessel-specific wing widths. Fishing Power Corrections are applied to catches from the ODNR R/V *Explorer* (1988–2002) and *Explorer* (2003–present; same name, different vessel) to correct those vessels' fishing power to the OMNRF R/V *Keenosay* (Tyson et al. 2006). Catch-per-hectare is then extrapolated up to country- and depth-specific strata area and then divided by the total basin area to yield a basinwide abundance estimate (in fish per hectare).

## Trawl Effort
![](figures/maps/2023 effort map.png)

Ontario and Ohio combined to attempt `r effort_summary$trawl_sites` trawl sites in August `r this_year`, of which `r effort_summary$low_do_sites` sites were removed due to hypoxia (<2.0 mg/L; blue points) and `r effort_summary$bad_trawl_sites` were removed due to gear issues. In total, `r effort_summary$good_trawl_sites` sites were used in this year's index calculations.

\newpage

## Walleye Indices

### Young-of-year index
![Young-of-year Walleye catch per hectare, Western Basin Lake Erie](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 334_1.png)
The Western Basin YOY Walleye index in `r this_year` was moderate (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "334_1")]` fish/ha) compared to recent years but strong compared to the overall time series. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "334_1")]` greatest year class since 1988.

### Young-of-year catch map
![](figures/maps/percid indices/age-0 334 map.png)

Catches of age-0 Walleye were concentrated in Ontario waters, spread across the central and eastern portions of their jurisdiction. Ohio catches have been transformed to R/V *Keenosay* catch efficiency using FPCs.

### Yearling index
![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 334_2.png)

The yearling Walleye index was also moderate (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "334_2")]` fish/ha) compared to recent years but strong compared to the overall time series. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "334_2")]` greatest yearling year class since 1988.
\newpage

## Yellow Perch Indices

### Young-of-year index
![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 331_1.png)

The Western Basin YOY Yellow Perch index in `r this_year` was somewhat low compared to the last 10 years (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "331_1")]` fish/ha) but was moderately strong compared to the time series. This is the `r ranks$rank[which(ranks$spp_agegroup == "331_1")]` greatest year class since 1988.

### Young-of-year catch map
![](figures/maps/percid indices/age-0 331 map.png)

Catches of age-0 Yellow Perch were concentrated in Ontario waters, particularly near Pidgeon Bay (west of Point Pelee). Ohio catches have been transformed to R/V *Keenosay* catch efficiency using FPCs.

## Total Forage Index

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance by forage group.png)

Total forage density in `r this_year` was typical of the last five years (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "all_forage")]` fish/ha) and somewhat greater than last year. As usual, forage makeup was dominated by spiny-rayed prey (e.g., White Perch, Yellow Perch, and Walleye; `r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "spiny_ray")]` fish/ha). Note that 2021 catches were skewed due to a hypoxia-related outlier catch.

\newpage

## Major Forage Species Indices
### Young-of-year White Perch

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 301_1.png)

YOY White Perch abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "301_1")]` fish/ha) was somewhat high compared to recent years - about two-thirds of the ten-year mean abundance (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "301_1")]` fish/ha).


### Young-of-year Gizzard Shad

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 63_1.png)

YOY Gizzard Shad abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "63_1")]` fish/ha) was average compared to recent years but low compared to the time series;  abundance was down compared to the ten-year mean (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "63_1")]` fish/ha).

\newpage

### Young-of-year Emerald Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 196_1.png)

YOY Emerald Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "196_1")]` fish/ha) remained minimal in `r this_year`, continuing a decade-long trend of low abundance for this historically-important forage fish. Shiner abundance is likely to remain low while the adult Walleye population is large (Knight and Vondracek 1993).

### Adult Emerald Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 196_3.png)

Adult (ages-1+) Emerald Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "196_3")]` fish/ha) also remained minimal, continuing a decade-long trend of low abundance.

\newpage

### Round Goby

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 366_5.png)

Round Goby abundance across all ages (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "366_5")]` fish/ha) has declined for two years, about half of the 10 year mean (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "366_5")]` fish/ha).

\newpage

## Other Catches of Note
### Young-of-year White Bass

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 302_1.png)

YOY White Bass abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "302_1")]` fish/ha) rebounded from recent lows, although abundance remains low compared to the ten year mean (`r abund$ten_year_mean[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "302_1")]` fish/ha)

### Young-of-year Freshwater Drum

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 371_1.png)

YOY Freshwater Drum abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "371_1")]` fish/ha) was low compared to recent years, continuing a pattern of booms and busts.


### Young-of-year Trout-perch

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 291_1.png)

YOY Trout Perch abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "291_1")]` fish/ha) was also high, the second greatest year class since 2005.

### Adult Trout-perch

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 291_3.png)

Adult Trout Perch were also found in high abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "291_3")]` fish/ha) was also high, the largest catches since 2005.

### Young-of-year Silver Chub

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 191_1.png)

YOY Silver Chub abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "191_1")]` fish/ha) was very high in `r this_year`, the greatest year class since 1999.

### Young-of-year Mimic Shiner

![](figures/markdown/markdown abundance 206_1.png)

YOY Mimic Shiner abundance (`r abund$abundance[which(abund$spp_agegroup == "206_1")]` fish/ha) continued its climb, having increased every year for the last five.

\newpage
